reason: The dividing basal cells need nutrients to renew the skin, so these look like a natural pair.
expectation: They should produce new skin cells or a renewed skin layer.

effect: The basal cells produced new skin cells, showing the start of skin renewal.
reaction: The upward movement of older cells makes the renewal process clear.
reason: Erythropoietin is shown carrying a kidney signal to the red-cell precursors in marrow.
expectation: The signal should help the precursors produce new red blood cells.

effect: The kidney signal leads the marrow precursors toward red-cell maturation, connecting oxygen supply to blood renewal.
reaction: The low-oxygen cue makes the reason for the signal clearer.
reason: The two bone cell types are shown removing old matrix and depositing new matrix in the resulting hollow.
expectation: Together they should produce renewed bone tissue.

effect: The bone-removing cells cannot combine with anything yet, so bone renewal may require another step first.
reaction: I am unsure what enables the bone cells to act.
reason: The new skin cells appear ready to contribute to renewal in the body.
expectation: The new cells should renew the body's skin.

alternatives.reason: Checking the body's available partners could clarify the renewal sequence.

effect: The new cells renewed the body's skin, showing how cells made below replace those shed at the surface.
reaction: The connection between cell production and shedding is clear.
reason: The developing red cells appear ready to add blood renewal to the same body.
expectation: The body will gain a supply of newly developing red blood cells.

effect: The developing red cells added blood renewal to the body, linking marrow production with the kidney’s low-oxygen signal.
reaction: Seeing the red cells leave marrow for a vessel makes the connection concrete.
reason: The bone-removing cells could not act earlier, but the body now has skin and blood renewal in place. I will try them with the updated body.
expectation: The bone-removing cells should begin replacing an old patch of bone.

effect: The bone-removing cells act on the body first, creating a patch ready for the next stage of renewal.
reaction: That explains why combining the two bone cell types directly did not work.
reason: The bone-forming cells are shown depositing new matrix in the hollow left by bone removal.
expectation: The cells should add new bone matrix to the patch and complete bone renewal.

effect: Bone-forming cells completed the renewal sequence, showing that different cells remove and rebuild bone matrix.
reaction: The final result made the two stages of bone renewal clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding developing red cells to the body was worthwhile because it connected marrow production to the kidney's response to low oxygen.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to combine the two bone cell types was confusing at first; their descriptions suggested they worked in sequence, but did not make the required interaction with the body clear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the bone-removing cells had to act on the body before the bone-forming cells could rebuild the patch.

arbitrary.text: The required order for adding the renewal processes to the body was not clear from the initial board. The failed bone-cell combination made that especially noticeable.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in another chapter if it explored a new relationship or presented a less predictable problem. The renewal examples were clear, though much of this chapter involved pairing described components and adding them to the body.
